title: Composition or cell state? Decomposing the adenoma-carcinoma transcriptome across tissue, epithelium and single cells - reproducibility package
description:
Reproducible analysis code and derived intermediate results for a study that re-attributes the transcriptomic shift along the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence to epithelial-intrinsic versus stromal-compositional components.

The package contains no new primary data. Every script operates on public datasets from NCBI GEO (GSE41258, GSE37364, GSE20916, GSE41657, GSE4183, GSE117606, GSE15960, GSE161277, GSE109308, GSE128435, GSE303070) and on derived tables written by earlier stages, so that every number, table and figure in the manuscript can be traced back to a script and an input file.

Stages: A consensus signature (Stouffer integration across discovery cohorts) - B drift diagnostics - C LCM-based compartment attribution - D three-layer pattern matrix - E sensitivity analysis - F single-cell P x U decomposition - G supplementary-table build - H figure rendering - I manuscript artefact assembly.

The five CSV products of the upstream R pipeline (limma / WGCNA) are shipped under upstream_r/ so that the Python package is self-contained. See REPRODUCIBILITY.md for the full script-to-artefact mapping, and README.md for the environment and quick-start instructions. Released under the MIT License.

v1.0.3 fixes one line: the README archived-version row had a doubled https://doi.org/ prefix and named the previous release. It now points at the concept DOI, which always resolves to the newest version.

Changes in v1.0.2 (reproducibility audit; no reported number, table or figure changed). Two scripts no longer resolve their working directory from a developer-local absolute path. Inputs that earlier stages read but that had never been shipped are now included: consensus_signature_tier.csv, manuscript_facts.py, epithelial_core_genes.json, stromal_layer_genes.json, cohort_hunt2.py, gpl_soft_map.py and collide_results.json. The classifier module matters most: without it the sample classifier silently degraded to substring matching, which merged one cohort's carcinoma group into other and wrote truncated results with exit code 0. three_layer_check.py now refuses to overwrite archived results when a cohort was skipped (it writes *.partial.json and exits 2), and drift_diag.json is regenerated under the shipped code. REQUIREMENTS.txt pins Pillow and states explicitly that figure bytes additionally depend on the FreeType build that Matplotlib links against, which no pip pin can control. REPRODUCIBILITY.md section 9 gives the data-preparation order, the working route for the one platform whose annotation is absent from GEO, and exactly which artefacts are byte-identical and which are only semantically identical.

The development version of this package is maintained at github.com/Yao204-116/crc-adenoma-carcinoma-compartment-attribution.
